{"self_assessment":"Impact: I stocked the shared bin early with a full 40-domino load, so the table never ran short while the fish went up. I then laid the bottom line of the body from the start out to the belly, and fixed the join at the start so the bottom line received the fall along with the top. That meant the whole outline fell from a single push, and I confirmed it by eye at 143 of 143 dominoes connected. I also extended the lower tail fork from the body end and stood a fallen domino back up.

Execution: I worked from the scratch pad sketch and traced my stroke in small, steady batches. I inspected the joins several times, around the belly, the tail and the lower fork, to find breaks before the push. I flagged the break at the bend of the lower fork, where one domino sat off the line. In the last few minutes I kept hands off so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I agreed a clean split on the bottom line with Priya, so we weren't working on top of each other. I stopped at the belly and she took the back half. When she asked me to hang back from the lower fork, I did, and I moved to checking the tail joins. I offered help where it was useful and kept the table updated on what was connected.

Leadership: I called out the plan for my section, kept the group coordinated on who held which part, and pushed for hands off before the push to protect the finished fish. I kept communication clear and steady through the build.

I believe my share of the table's result was about 30 percent.","my_share_percent":30}
